text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Environment Minister Angela Merkel insists transport of nuclear waste to storage unit in northern Germany cannot be postponed or cancelled.
- Sources in ruling Christian Democrats suggest pensions could be cut more quickly than foreseen in Labour Minister Norbert Bluem's plans.
- Justice minister of Rhineland-Palatinate state warns of poor career prospects for law students.
- Government wants more private finance for transport projects.
HANDELSBLATT
- German railway company Deutsche Bahn sees itself on track for success, plans to cut 24,000 jobs in 1997.
- Justice ministry says cloning of humans is forbidden under German law.
- Warnings of cancer risks on side of cigarette packets are legal, Federal Constitutional Court rules.
- Deutsche Telekom does not plan to float any more shares on stock market before the end of the century.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann plans first ever tolls on German roads.
- Lufthansa pilots vote to strike.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl speaks out in favour of competition among German universities.
- Volkswagen urges suppliers to support its drive against corruption allegations in the sector.
DIE WELT
- Optimism prevalent in Bonn ahead of next round of talks on tax reform between government and opposition.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) call on government to postpone vote on capital trading tax.
- Retailers hope for boost of between 10 and 12 billion marks from tax reform plans.
- Decision expected before end of March on future of subsidies for German coal industry.
